$comment: Widget profile, the contract every client enforces (docs/decisions.md, "Profile v1"). The single source: packages/core/scripts/profile-build.ts generates src/shared/profile-tables.ts (the validator, the shim, the renderer) and docs/profile-v1.md from it. Seeded 2026-10-17 from packages/conformance/catalogue.json with the decisions of that day; a widget detects it at runtime (TelegramWidget.profile, isProfileAtLeast, CSS.supports, @supports).

decisions.D3: A feature is in when every client draws it; :hover and user-select: text are the exceptions (progressive enhancement: where a client lacks them, the widget still works)
decisions.D3a: v1: canvas 2D; Web Animations, filter, backdrop-filter if clients draw them; out: forms, inner scroll, 3D transforms, magic move; CSS animations and transitions in
decisions.D3b: Fonts: system generic families only, other names dropped
decisions.D4: Input: taps in the PoC, drag in v1; no keyboard at all, not even Enter or Space (it conflicts with the chat input field; Artem, 2026-10-16)
decisions.D5: strict policy everywhere; webAnimations and morphUpdates from the profile
decisions.D8: SDK outward: openLink (confirmed with the full URL) and openTelegramLink (no confirmation of its own, 2026-10-29) on a tap, haptics; no sendMessage
decisions.D11: One widget model: classic DOM in the sandbox
decisions.D12a: Above the cap: hard clip, no fullscreen
decisions.D17: State: localStorage per (account, chat, message id): the chat the message is in, as message ids are unique only within a chat (supergroups); 4 KB, QuotaExceededError; sessionStorage in memory
decisions.D18: Text is not selectable by default; a widget enables selection with user-select: text (2026-10-20, replaces "Text selection forbidden")
decisions.D20: Mini-HTML (2026-10-17): a widget is one HTML document of at most 4 KB compressed and 32 KB uncompressed, delivered in the message; the server compresses the HTML from the bot (zlib at level 9 since 2026-10-24) and enforces both limits
decisions.D23: Runtime profile detection: TelegramWidget.profile / isProfileAtLeast, CSS.supports and @supports from the profile
decisions.inv1: Invariant 1: widget JS only in QuickJS
decisions.inv2: Invariant 2: the host validates everything against the allowlists
decisions.inv4: Invariant 4: only data: images, host blob: and #fragment URLs reach the renderer
decisions.P1: Profile v1 freeze (2026-10-17): a candidate is in when the corpus uses it and the web renderers draw it; the rest are out until the native renderers are measured (profile 2)
decisions.P1-grid: Grid is in on condition that the Swift renderer and TwidgetCore implement it before their releases (2026-10-17)
decisions.P1-ua: Clarified in v0.1.1 (2026-10-20): the renderer's user-agent layer (tables.uaStylesheet) also fixes the root and the text elements: the bubble's text colour (the bubble's own fill is the canvas behind a transparent renderer), the client's text tokens (--tg-text-font-size, --tg-text-line-height, --tg-text-padding as the body's margin) and explicit sizes and margins for headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, quotes and code, so a UA default in this profile means that layer, not an engine's own stylesheet
decisions.SDK: SDK v1 (docs/sdk-v1.md), with Artem's answers of 2026-10-17: haptics without a gesture (bucket 5, 10 per second), any t.me path, URLs of at most 256 characters, 16 handlers per event type, stopped after 2 crashes in a row, double tap and long press stay with the bubble (replaced by G1 in v0.1.2)
decisions.G1: Gestures, v0.1.2 (Artem, 2026-10-22): one shared policy with the same thresholds on every client and in the sandbox. A double tap over the widget is always the widget's (both clicks and dblclick, on every element; the reaction stays with the bubble outside the widget). For the rest touch-action is the claim, decided per element at pointerdown over the target and its ancestors (a container covers its children, as in CSS): auto: holds and swipes are the bubble's (the widget gets pointercancel); pan-y / pan-x: drags on the other axis are the widget's; none: everything is the widget's, holds (contextmenu) included. The leading 20 px of the widget and the bubble outside it never take a claim. Replaces "double tap and long press stay with the bubble" (SDK)
decisions.G2: Vertical drags are the chat's, v0.1.3 (Artem, 2026-10-24): a widget claims only horizontal drags; a vertical drag over a widget always scrolls the chat, whatever touch-action says, and the widget gets pointercancel. auto: holds and drags are the bubble's; pan-y: horizontal drags are the widget's; pan-x claims nothing; none: horizontal drags and holds (contextmenu) are the widget's. The axis lock (the first move past the 10 px slop decides for the whole press), double taps and the leading 20 px are unchanged. The engine under the renderer always allows vertical panning. Replaces G1's pan-x and the vertical half of none
decisions.R1: Resize anchor, v0.1.3 (Artem, 2026-10-24): TelegramWidget.setResizeAnchor('top' | 'bottom') says which edge of the bubble stays put on screen when the widget's height changes (top by default: it grows downward; bottom: it grows upward and the content above moves). An SDK v1 addition inside profile 1: TelegramWidget.profile stays 1 and widgets detect the method with typeof. It goes through the bridge as a checked call (sdk-policy, four copies and the fixture), needs no gesture, and the host keeps the latest value and reports it with the height; the client's list compensates its scroll
decisions.I1: The bot's data and requests (Artem, 2026-10-25; the server's spec): a widget is fixed code plus changeable state: the HTML never changes after sending; the state changes, and only the bot writes it. TelegramWidget.chatData, the chat state (one original message, seen only in its chat: in a group every member sees it; never forwarded), and publicData, the shared state (wherever the widget is shown: a forward gets a copy, or shares a shared widget's one state with the original): each a text of up to 1024 bytes (UTF-8), read-only in the widget; chatDataChanged / publicDataChanged when they change (no restart). isForward, chatType and viewer (Mini Apps' WebAppUser: id, first_name, last_name, username, is_premium; a field that breaks its rule is left out); a forward is told nothing about the chat it is in (no chatType: the bot must not learn where its widget was forwarded), and the widget knows its viewer only where it may ask the bot (can_query), originals included. request(data of 1-64 bytes): a callback button inside the widget; where it may ask is the server's per message (can_query: originals of a widget sent with allow_queries, forwards of one sent with fwd_allow_queries; background_query: the original in the private chat with the bot); the client marks a widget with can_query as one whose tap may send data to the bot's server; on a tap, one per tap (shared with openLink, openTelegramLink and copyText); in the background while visible: one when the widget appears on screen, then one per 5 s; one in flight; resolves { result } (text of at most 1024 bytes), rejects with error.code; the answer does not change the state. copyText(text of 1-256 characters) on a tap; the client's toast shows what it copied. Part of SDK v1 and layer 233 from the launch, inside profile 1. TelegramWidget.isPreview: an inline result in the list before it is sent gets its state but no input, no bridge call but ready and setResizeAnchor, no chat type or viewer, and Web Storage that is never committed. The checks are sdk-policy (four copies and the fixture)
decisions.L1: Strict limits from the start (2026-10-29): about twice what real widgets use; past a counted cap the widget stops (docs/decisions.md)
decisions.L2: Heavy boxes (Artem, 2026-11-02, after the client teams' stress-kit runs on five devices): at most 16 heavy boxes at once (a blurred box-shadow layer, a filter, a backdrop-filter, opacity below 1 but a disabled or pressed <button>'s, or a running animation of filter, backdrop-filter or opacity, or of box-shadow through a blurred layer), of them at most 2 with backdrop-filter; every renderer counts on the computed style (packages/core/src/shared/paint-policy.ts and its fixture) and past either the widget stops. A tightening of profile 1 (widgets were not launched yet), not profile 2
decisions.P1-safe-area: Clarified on 2026-10-29 (Artem; widgets were not launched yet), not profile 2: a client draws the message time and its status over the bottom corner of a widget with no caption below it, as on a photo (with a caption below the time is in the caption's line and nothing is drawn over the widget; a caption shown above the widget, invert_media, is as none: Artem's decision of 2026-10-30). env(safe-area-inset-top|right|bottom|left[, fallback]) is in: the validator rewrites it to var(--tg-content-safe-area-inset-…[, fallback]), root variables the renderer sets like the theme's (bottom = the height of the time's band, the others 0), with --tg-content-safe-area-corner-left|right for the width of the client's corner in that band (a physical side: right in a left-to-right interface, left in a right-to-left one); 0 with a caption below. Another env() name resolves to its fallback or drops the declaration. The UA layer adds the band to the body's bottom padding, and TelegramWidget.contentSafeAreaInset with the contentSafeAreaChanged event gives the same numbers to script

features.title: TelegramWidget.chatData and publicData: the widget's chat state and shared state, which only the bot writes (read-only, null for none, each a text of up to 1024 bytes in UTF-8); chatDataChanged / publicDataChanged when they change
features.note: The chat state (chatData) is tied to one original message and seen only in its chat (in a group every member sees it), and is null in a forward; the shared state (publicData) is seen wherever the widget is shown: a static widget's forward gets a copy as of the forward, a shared widget (widget_id) has one for all its messages and forwards; the widget cannot change either, only ask the bot (request); one change of both fires both, chat first; an unchanged value fires nothing.

features.title: TelegramWidget.isForward, chatType and viewer (a WebAppUser): a forwarded copy, the kind of chat, who looks; no chatType in a forward, no viewer where the widget may not ask the bot
features.note: viewer is shaped like Mini Apps' WebAppUser (id, first_name, last_name, username, is_premium only when true; names 1-64 UTF-16 code units, a username 5-32 of [A-Za-z0-9_]; a field that breaks its rule is left out); chatType is private, group, supergroup or channel and null in every forward (a copy is told nothing about its chat); viewer only where the message has can_query (an original sent with allow_queries, a forward of one sent with fwd_allow_queries), else null.

features.title: TelegramWidget.request(data): a callback button inside the widget; data of 1-64 bytes, resolves { result } (text of at most 1024 bytes), rejects with error.code; where it may ask is the server's flag per message
features.note: On a tap where can_query (originals of a widget sent with allow_queries, forwards of one sent with fwd_allow_queries; the client shows a network marker there), in the background only where background_query (the original in the private chat with the bot) while visible: one when the widget appears on screen, then one per 5 s; one in flight; the answer does not change the state.

features.title: TelegramWidget.copyText(text): copies 1-256 characters on a tap; the client's toast shows the copied text
features.note: One call per tap, shared with the links and request; outside a tap dropped with activation-blocked; navigator.clipboard stays a stub.

features.title: TelegramWidget.watchPublicData() / unwatchPublicData(): the widget asks to follow its shared state live; the client polls a shared widget's shared state (public_data) only while it watches and is on screen
features.note: No tap needed, idempotent; the shim sends only changes and the host keeps the latest (web onWatchPublicData and watchesPublicData, the native diagnostics); a widget that does not watch gets its shared state with the message and the bot's pushed edits only; a preview never watches.

features.title: A widget with no caption below it (none, or one shown above it) gets the message time and status over its bottom corner, on a backing as on a photo, and taps on it are the client's; the client passes the band (contentSafeArea bottom) and its corner (cornerRight, or cornerLeft in a right-to-left interface) before the first render and changes them only with the bubble's layout (a caption added, removed or moved above or below by an edit, "edited"); with a caption below the time is in the caption's line and the safe area is 0

features.title: A change of the widget's state reaches the running widget as chatDataChanged / publicDataChanged (the client's setData with the full state: the server's update, or the polled shared state): no new host, no restart
features.note: The client keeps the state with the message; a shared widget's shared state (public_data, widget_id) is polled for one visible carrier per id, one message per call, at the object's period and applied to every widget with that id, forwards included; an answer does not change the state; testable with a test bot once the server ships.

features.title: A forwarded copy never has a chat state (chatData); its shared state (publicData) is a copy as of the forward or a shared widget's one shared state; it is told nothing about the chat it is in (no chatType); it asks the bot only on a tap and only if the widget was sent with fwd_allow_queries, and otherwise has no viewer either
features.note: The client passes the server's flags (is_copy, can_query); the framework drops chatData and chatType of a copy, and viewer of any message without can_query.

features.title: A widget in a list of inline results is a preview: the client creates it with context.preview and the result's state, routes no touches to it (a tap selects the result) and creates a new host for the sent message
features.note: The host drops the preview's input, every bridge call but ready and setResizeAnchor, and its storage commits; chatType and viewer are null.

features.title: The network marker: the client marks a widget whose tap may send data to the bot's server exactly where the message has can_query (a UI contract of the server's spec)
features.note: Never without allow_queries, never on a forward of a widget without fwd_allow_queries, never on a preview; the client's own UI from context.canQuery (docs/integration.md).
